name: NY-24
label: Likely R

key_factors: No polls or expert ratings; markets price ~7% for Democrats
model.rationale: The R+11 lean, Tenney's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and Polymarket pricing Democrats at roughly 7% all point to a comfortable Republican hold with minimal evidence of a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Ellman within single digits, or a major Tenney scandal or outside spending surge, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Claudia Tenney seeks another term in a central New York district that leans Republican by about eleven points on recent partisan performance. She enters the general election as a well-funded incumbent, having raised roughly $2.8 million and holding about $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Alissa Ellman has raised under $200,000 with little cash remaining. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race on either side.

There are no public general-election polls and no expert rating organizations have weighed in, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and the financial imbalance. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a 7 percent chance. The forecast calls the race Likely Republican, with Tenney favored by roughly fifteen points and modest residual uncertainty given the absence of polling.
